text: Continuous integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers add new code to a shared project, automated builds start immediately. These builds check that the code compiles correctly and that everything works together. As part of the same process, the system runs tests automatically. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. CI pipelines usually include several steps, such as building, testing, and reporting results. If something fails, developers get quick feedback and can fix it right away. As a result, the software stays more reliable, and the whole team can work faster with less stress.
